svg.text: grey faceted rock, snow on the shade side, conifers low down, scree
A. At fight distance, noon: the ground profile, the cover silhouettes, the far land as a value ladder. The two grey figures are 75 units tall (a fighter): scale only, no character art.
Palette at noon (the world-light tint per sky key multiplies it; lit, mid and shade are the three faces of one surface; the far ladder is each ridge hazed toward the horizon)

Readability (docs/art/dynamic-sky.md section 6): worst aura against any tone 20.8 CIEDE2000 (rule: 20 or more), worst Protagonist or rival body against ground, rock or vegetation 23.1 (rule: 15 or more), over every sky key with the world-light tint.
B. What the fight leaves: scorched (a beam along the ground), cratered (an impact), burned (fire on what grows)
a black soot streak along the rock, snow on it melted to a dark wet line,
the scree glassy in the middle
a bowl in broken rock, the rim a ring of angular blocks and a skirt of
conifers charred black, snow patches grey with soot, bare pale rock where
C. Destruction in mountains: the impact at three moments (burst, peak, settle). Rock shards: angular chunks on long arcs and a grey dust cloud; on a slope the scree slides downhill for two seconds.
D. Where it meets its neighbours (hard steps in colour, never a fade; the cover mixes over about a third of the width)
Foothills: the hills rise in steps, rock outcrops through the grass, fir groves
The tree line climbs the slope: tall firs, then small firs, then scree and rock.
A cloud forest: the canopy stays but the ridges rise behind it, darker; ferns on
Badlands: red mesas and scree fans spill from the grey rock; no soil between.
The rock turns from grey to black, ash slopes replace scree, a cone stands
Bare rock above, lichen and stunted scrub below, snow in the folds.
Glacier tongues run down between the rock ridges; the snow line is a hard step.
